newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Political uncertainty sends Seoul shrs to end down.
newsitem.headline: Political uncertainty sends Seoul shrs to end down.

text.p: Shares ended Wednesday's trading lower after political uncertainty over the Hanbo scandal sparked late afternoon selling, brokers said.
The composite stock index fell 3.10 points to close at 679.71. Decliners beat advancers 433 to 349.
Brokers said investors are worried that political instability will further undermine the staggering stock market.
"The political situation is starting to outweigh economic issues," said Choi Tae-hwan, head of sales at KLB Securities.
Trading had started strongly, as rumours of a raise in the foreign shareholding ceiling and news of an expansion of the Korea Fund's paid-in capital helped sentiment.

The finance ministry has denied talk that the government may raise the foreign limit as early as April 1. The limit is currently set at 20 percent. This will be raised to 23 percent some time this year, but no schedule has yet been set.
On Tuesday, the ministery announced it would boost Korea Fund's paid-in capital by $200 million in May to $580 million to attract foreign funds.
Selected blue chips rose. Korea Mobile Telecom gained 20,000 won to 500,000. LG Electronics rose 200 won to 11,500.
"It is hard to predict how the market is going to move tomorrow, because it all depends on what news comes out about Hanbo and other political issues," said a local broker.
"Investors are going to wait and see what happens."
Hanbo Steel racked up $5.8 billion in debts before going under on January 23. Prosecutors said banks were pressured by politicians to offer huge loans.
Market fundamentals remain far from strong.
Interest rates, though retreating from recent highs, are still strong. Three-year corporate bonds ended Tuesday's trading at 12.37 percent.
Customer deposits at brokerages, as of Saturday, fell 0.68 of a percent from Friday to 2.9 billion won, while loans for margin trading rose 0.62 of a percent to 2.87 billion.
March futures contracts fell 0.50 of a point to 68.70, while the KOSPI 200 index lost 0.45 of a point to 70.02.
